correctness.rationale: Every permissible word of length L gives a directed trail of L-3 distinct nonpalindromic four-letter edges in the order-three de Bruijn digraph and uses at most one member of each reversal pair. The 64-vertex flow, binary pair constraints, and endpoint choices yield a 368-variable, 186-row integer-program relaxation even without connectivity; its optimum upper-bounds every word. Independently rebuilt the matrix from all 240 allowed four-grams and solved with SciPy HiGHS: status optimal, objective -110, certified MIP dual bound -110, zero relative gap; the displayed literal word has 113 letters and all 110 windows are distinct, nonpalindromic and pairwise non-reversals. This proves L_4(4)=113 conditional on correct MILP solver bound; no separate machine-checked rational optimality proof is claimed.
residual_risks: MILP optimizer reported global dual bound rather than independently verified formal cutting-plane proof; solver-dependent finite computational correctness remains.
Earlier finite quaternary orientable-word tables or analogous integer programs may be unindexed.
